title: Splitwise Multi-Currency & Groups
description: Handle exchange rate complexities, group splitting strategies, recurring expenses, and payment settlement integration.

segments.text: A group trip across Europe: hotel in euros, dinner in pounds, taxi in Swiss francs. When settling up, which currency do you use? Exchange rates fluctuate. Splitwise converts all expenses to a base currency at the time of entry, but this creates discrepancies when rates change between expense and settlement.

Exchange rate handling options: convert at time of expense — simple but settlement may differ. Convert at time of settlement — fair but requires tracking original currencies. Or let users choose their settlement currency. Store all amounts in original currency plus the converted amount and the rate used. This provides an audit trail.

Exchange rate data comes from APIs like Open Exchange Rates or European Central Bank. Cache rates with a one-hour TTL — rates don't change by the second for consumer use. For amounts under one thousand dollars, mid-market rates are fine. For larger amounts, consider showing a warning about potential rate differences from actual bank rates.

Groups have membership management: add members, remove members, transfer ownership. When a member leaves a group with outstanding debts, their balance must be settled first. Block removal until balance is zero or the group creator approves a write-off. Group archiving preserves history without cluttering the active view.
A roommate group has a new member joining mid-month. They shouldn't pay for utilities from before they moved in. How do you handle partial-month membership in recurring expense splitting?
segments.thought_prompt: How do you handle a new group member who shouldn't pay for expenses before their join date?

segments.text: Recurring expenses — rent, utilities, subscriptions — auto-create expenses on a schedule. Define: amount, frequency, payer rotation, and split ratio. Monthly rent of three thousand split among three roommates creates a new expense on the first of each month. Support payer rotation where each roommate takes turns paying. Track the rotation state in the recurring expense definition.

Settlement integration lets users pay debts directly through the app. Integrate with Venmo, PayPal, or bank transfers via Plaid. When a settlement payment is confirmed, update the debt graph atomically. Handle partial settlements — a user can settle fifty of the one hundred they owe. Mark the payment and reduce the balance accordingly.

Notification strategy: notify on new expenses involving the user, weekly balance summary, reminders for overdue debts — configurable threshold, and settlement confirmations. Avoid notification fatigue — batch notifications for groups with frequent expenses. Allow per-group notification preferences and quiet hours.

The complete data model: Users table, Groups table with membership junction, Expenses table with payer and split participants, Debts table materialized from expenses for fast balance queries, Settlements table tracking payments, and ExchangeRates table for historical rate lookup. Materialize the debt graph on write to avoid expensive re-computation on read.

Design the complete backend for a Splitwise-like app supporting ten million users, multi-currency, recurring expenses, and real-time balance updates. What are your key data model and API design decisions?
segments.thought_prompt: Design Splitwise backend for 10M users with multi-currency and recurring expenses.

segments.text: Multi-currency expense splitting requires careful exchange rate management with audit trails. Groups need membership lifecycle with debt-blocking on removal. Recurring expenses automate routine splitting with payer rotation. Settlement integration closes the loop from tracking to payment. The data model materializes debts on write for fast balance reads.
